title: Southlake
name: Southlake
metaTitle: Southlake 1031 Exchange Investors | Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Southlake investors trading Town Square retail and office, and corporate-adjacent space near Sabre's headquarters campus.

sections.html: Southlake built its commercial identity around Southlake Town Square, an open-air lifestyle center that combines retail, restaurants, office space, and the town's own municipal buildings inside one walkable footprint. That integration changes how a lease or ownership interest inside the square should be documented compared with a standalone retail center elsewhere in the metro. An exchanger who assumes every Southlake commercial parcel is privately owned in the conventional sense risks missing an obligation that only shows up in the square's own governing documents.

sections.heading: Town Square's Mixed Public-Private Footprint Requires Its Own Documentation Check
sections.html: Because Southlake's city hall and public library sit inside the same development as its retail and office space, an exchanger should confirm which parcels are privately held and separately deeded versus which are subject to shared-facility or common-area agreements tied to the square's original planned development agreement with the city. That agreement can carry maintenance or design obligations a standard retail lease does not. Requesting a copy of that governing document directly from the town or the square's management office, rather than relying on a title company's general commitment, is the more reliable way to confirm what obligations actually attach to a specific unit.

sections.heading: Property Types Available to a Southlake Exchanger
sections.html:
The commercial stock here includes several distinct categories:

  • retail and restaurant space inside Southlake Town Square's open-air footprint
  • office suites above Town Square retail, some leased to professional services firms
  • corporate office space near the Sabre Corporation campus and surrounding office parks
  • boutique and specialty retail along the corridors surrounding the square
  • a limited stock of standalone net-lease retail parcels along the town's major arterials

Corporate-adjacent office space near the Sabre campus has historically leased at a premium tied to that proximity, and confirming current occupancy at the campus itself is a reasonable diligence step before assuming that premium will hold through a new hold period.

sections.heading: Identification Strategy Around a Concentrated Corporate-Tenant Market
sections.html: Office product near a large corporate campus like Sabre's carries concentration risk if a significant share of nearby leasing depends on that single employer's presence. An exchanger exiting this kind of asset often benefits from the 200% rule to keep Town Square retail or a DST interest available as an alternative rather than staying locked into a three-property list of similar corporate-adjacent office. A DST interest diversified across several office or retail holdings can also reduce reliance on any single Southlake employer's continued presence.

sections.heading: Planned Development Agreement Terms Belong in the Improvement Exchange File
sections.html: Any renovation or expansion inside Town Square should be checked against the original planned development agreement's design standards before construction begins. The square's cohesive architectural look is a contractual obligation tied to that agreement, not an informal expectation, and an improvement exchange timeline should account for that design review before counting on the 180-day period to run without delay. Any signage or storefront change should be submitted through the same design review process regardless of how minor the change appears, since even a modest awning replacement can trigger review if it alters the building's approved elevation.

sections.heading: Coordinating Closing Where a Shared-Facility Agreement Is Part of the Record
sections.html: The qualified intermediary's exchange agreement and the title company's commitment should both reference any shared-facility or common-area agreement tied to Town Square. A title exam that misses this document can produce a closing package that omits an obligation the buyer discovers only after taking title. Confirming the shared-facility agreement's maintenance-cost allocation before closing also prevents a buyer from inheriting an assessment dispute that predates their ownership.

faqs.q: Does buying retail space inside Southlake Town Square involve more than a standard lease and deed?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The square's original planned development agreement with the city can carry shared-facility, maintenance, or design obligations, and confirming those terms should happen before closing, not after.

faqs.q: How many properties should I identify exiting office space near the Sabre corporate campus?
faqs.a: More than three is common when a significant share of nearby leasing activity is tied to one large employer, since the 200% rule lets an investor include Town Square retail or a DST interest as a diversification option.

faqs.q: Do I need approval before renovating a Southlake Town Square storefront?
faqs.a: In most cases the square's design standards, set by its planned development agreement, require review before construction begins, and that review should be documented and built into the improvement exchange timeline.

faqs.q: Is Town Square office space directly comparable to standalone corporate office near Sabre for identification purposes?
faqs.a: They differ enough in ownership structure and lease terms that listing them side by side on an identification notice should be done carefully, with each property's documentation reviewed on its own record.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Fort Worth confirm whether my Southlake property qualifies for exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates documentation and scheduling among the investor's advisors. Qualification determinations rest with the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.

faqs.q: Does proximity to the Sabre corporate campus reliably support a leasing premium?
faqs.a: It has historically, but that premium depends on the campus maintaining its current occupancy, so confirming current tenancy at the campus itself is a reasonable check before relying on the premium to hold through a new hold period.

faqs.q: What happens if a Southlake replacement property is still under construction near the identification deadline?
faqs.a: The exchange agreement should specify a firm completion date backed by the contractor's schedule, and the qualified intermediary should confirm that date leaves enough of the 180-day period to close after substantial completion, rather than assuming the project will finish on time.
